questions.q: Plants make food by photosynthesis. Name the gas they take in from the air.
questions.explain: Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air through their leaves. They use it with water to make sugar in photosynthesis.

questions.q: Plants make food by photosynthesis. Name the source of energy they use.
questions.explain: Plants use light energy from sunlight to make food. Chlorophyll in the leaves absorbs the light.

questions.q: Good soil helps plants grow well. Identify what good soil contains.
choices: nutrients and a very low pH
questions.explain: Good soil contains the nutrients plants need, such as nitrogen and phosphorus. It also has a suitable pH, close to neutral for most plants.

questions.q: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water. State the products of photosynthesis.
questions.explain: In photosynthesis, carbon dioxide and water are changed into sugar and oxygen. The plant uses the sugar as food and gives out the oxygen.

questions.q: Chlorophyll is the green substance in leaves. State what chlorophyll absorbs.
questions.explain: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy. The plant uses this energy to make food by photosynthesis.

questions.q: Universal indicator turns green in a soil solution. Identify the type of soil.
questions.explain: Universal indicator is green in a neutral solution, at pH 7. So the soil is neutral.

questions.q: Universal indicator turns red in a soil solution. Identify the type of soil.
questions.explain: Universal indicator turns red in an acidic solution. So the soil is acidic.

questions.q: Red litmus paper turns blue in a soil solution. Identify the type of soil.
questions.explain: An alkali turns red litmus paper blue. So the soil is alkaline.

questions.q: A pH meter reads 5 in a soil solution. Identify the type of soil.
questions.explain: A pH below 7 means the solution is acidic. A reading of 5 shows the soil is acidic.

questions.q: A soil is alkaline. Predict the colour of universal indicator in its solution.
questions.explain: Universal indicator turns blue or purple in an alkaline solution. So it turns blue.

questions.q: A soil is neutral. Predict the pH meter reading for its solution.
questions.explain: A neutral solution has a pH of 7. Below 7 is acidic and above 7 is alkaline.

questions.q: Farmers add fertilisers to soil. State how fertilisers help plants.
questions.explain: Fertilisers add nutrients to the soil. With more nutrients, plants grow faster and bigger.

questions.q: Chemical fertilisers are rich in two nutrients. Name these nutrients.
questions.explain: Chemical fertilisers are rich in nitrogen and phosphorus. Plants need these nutrients to grow well.

questions.q: Rain washes chemical fertiliser from a farm into a pond. Predict the effect on the pond.
questions.explain: The fertiliser adds nutrients to the pond water. Algae use these nutrients and grow very quickly. This is called an algal bloom.

questions.q: A thick layer of algae covers a pond. State what it stops from reaching pond life.
questions.explain: A thick layer of algae blocks sunlight from reaching the plants below. When the algae die and rot, the water also loses oxygen, so fish and other pond life suffer.

questions.q: Excess chemical fertiliser washes into groundwater. State the effect on our drinking water.
questions.explain: The fertiliser chemicals dissolve in the groundwater. This pollutes the water we use for drinking.

questions.q: Slash-and-burn clears forest by cutting and burning trees. State one benefit of it.
questions.explain: Burning the trees leaves ashes. The ashes add nutrients to the soil for the crops. The other choices are problems, not benefits.

questions.q: Farmers use slash-and-burn to clear land. State one problem it causes.
questions.explain: With the trees gone, nothing holds the soil in place. Rain washes the soil away, which is called soil erosion.

questions.q: Slash-and-burn causes haze. State one health effect of haze.
questions.explain: Haze is smoke and fine dust in the air. Breathing it in can cause breathing difficulties.

questions.q: Pesticide is sprayed on soil. Explain why birds that eat earthworms are harmed.
questions.explain: Earthworms take in the pesticide from the soil. Birds that eat many earthworms build up the poison in their bodies and are harmed.

questions.q: Rain carries pesticides into a river. Predict which living things are harmed.
questions.explain: Pesticides are poisons. When rain carries them into a river, they harm the plants and animals that live in the river.

questions.q: Biological control uses natural enemies to kill pests. State one benefit of it.
questions.explain: Biological control uses living natural enemies instead of chemicals. So no chemicals end up in the crops.

questions.q: Biological control uses natural enemies to kill pests. State one problem of it.
questions.explain: Adding a natural enemy to an area can upset the food chain. It may also eat other animals or grow too many in number.

questions.q: The world needs more food every year. Explain why food production must improve.
questions.explain: The number of people in the world keeps growing, but the space for farms is limited. So more food has to be grown on the same land.

questions.q: Farmers plant good seedlings. State how this improves food production.
questions.explain: Good seedlings come from healthy plants with useful features. They grow into crops that are bigger and better.

questions.q: Hydroponics grows plants in a nutrient solution. State one disadvantage of hydroponics.
questions.explain: Hydroponics needs tanks, pumps, nutrient solutions and lighting. These are expensive to set up.

questions.q: Plant hormones are used on farms. State one use of plant hormones.
questions.explain: Plant hormones control how plants grow. Farmers use some of them to make fruits ripen.

questions.q: Some plant hormones are used as weedkillers. Explain why they are safe for crops.
choices: they kill crops but not weeds
they kill weeds but not crops
questions.explain: These hormone weedkillers are chosen to kill the weeds but not the crops. So they can be sprayed on a field of crops.

questions.q: Plants are grown in a nutrient solution with no soil. Name this method.
questions.explain: Growing plants in a nutrient solution with no soil is called hydroponics.

questions.q: Plant roots hang in the air and are sprayed with nutrient mist. Name this method.
questions.explain: Growing plants with their roots hanging in the air and sprayed with a nutrient mist is called aeroponics.

questions.q: Natural enemies of pests are used to kill the pests. Name this method.
questions.explain: Using the natural enemies of pests to kill the pests is called biological control.

questions.q: Trees are cut down and burned to clear land. Name this method.
questions.explain: Cutting down trees and burning them to clear land is called slash-and-burn.

questions.q: A farmer sprays a chemical to kill weeds. Name this chemical.
questions.explain: A chemical that kills weeds is a herbicide. A pesticide kills pests, and a fertiliser adds nutrients.

questions.q: Rotted plant matter is added to soil. Name this material.
questions.explain: Rotted plant matter is called compost. It adds nutrients to the soil naturally.

questions.q: A farmer uses biological control. Describe what the farmer does.
questions.explain: In biological control the farmer brings in natural enemies of the pests, such as ladybirds that eat aphids. The enemies kill the pests.
